decision: WF-091 implements which rule for a quote whose creator is a configured approver?

state.workflow: WF-091 route a discounted quote for standard approval
state.question: The research contains two statements about self-approval that do not agree. Which product rule should this workflow implement?
state.statement_a: If a designated approver creates a quote, and they're the only approver, the quote won't require approval. If there are multiple approvers, they'll be removed from the approval process.
state.statement_b: Approvers can't approve their own quotes.
other_sourced_facts: Assign up to 10 approvers to review quotes that match your configured filters.
If there's more than one approver, and one approver requests changes, every approver will need to approve the quote again when the quote is re-submitted.
Choose All approvers required or At least one approver required.

candidate_1.rule: At enrolment, if the quote's creator is one of the configured approvers: drop the creator from the approver list. If the list is then empty (they were the only one), the quote does not require approval at all and goes straight to publishable. If other approvers remain, they approve and the creator may not.
candidate_1.serves: Both halves of statement_a, and it makes statement_b true as a consequence.
candidate_1.cost: A single-approver discount policy approves every discount that approver authors. That is the policy an org with one approver chose.

candidate_2.rule: Every matching quote requires approval. The creator is always removed from the approver list. If that empties the list, the enrolment is refused with a named reason and the quote stays DRAFT and unshareable.
candidate_2.serves: Statement_b strictly, at the price of statement_a.
candidate_2.cost: Contradicts the researched behaviour outright. A room with one approver can never ship a discounted quote.

candidate_3.rule: Every matching quote requires approval and the creator can never vote. The workflow records both sourced sentences and exposes a per-rule setting choose_no_approval_when_author_is_sole_approver, default on.
candidate_3.serves: Statement_a as a configurable default and statement_b as the floor.
candidate_3.cost: Adds a setting the research does not describe. A default that silently bypasses a control is the thing a reviewer will not find.

constraints: Records are arbitrary JSON. No migration and no typed column.
The domain module imports nothing but the store.
Every write is audited and names a route the app serves.
The choice must be served on the page so a reader sees which reading was taken.

reason: selected 'sole_approver_author_needs_no_approval_multi_approver_drops_author' but confidence 0.44 < 0.70 (margin 0.27); options too close to decide on this evidence

criteria.sole_approver_author_needs_no_approval_m: Implement statement_a exactly. The sole-approver author needs no approval. With several approvers the author is dropped from the list.
criteria.always_require_approval_and_forbid_own_v: Every match requires approval and the author can never vote. An emptied approver list is refused.
criteria.record_both_and_expose_no_automatic_bypa: Every match requires approval and the author can never vote. A named per-rule toggle restores the sole-approver bypass and defaults on.

decision: WF-091 implements which self-approval rule, narrowed to two candidates with measured context?

state.workflow: WF-091 route a discounted quote for standard approval
state.refinement_of_audit: jev-20261005T064542-8564-42977 returned uncertain at confidence 0.44 across three candidates. Candidates are narrowed to the two that survived, and the evidence below is what I measured while implementing.
state.question: Which of these two rules should WF-091 implement for a quote whose creator is a configured approver?

conflicting_evidence.statement_a: If a designated approver creates a quote, and they're the only approver, the quote won't require approval. If there are multiple approvers, they'll be removed from the approval process.
conflicting_evidence.statement_b: Approvers can't approve their own quotes.

measured_context: The two statements do not contradict each other once enrolment is treated as the point of decision. Statement_a describes what happens to the approver LIST at enrolment. Statement_b describes who may cast a VOTE. Removing the creator from the list makes statement_b true by construction rather than by a second rule.

Statement_a gives the sole-approver case its own outcome, and it is the only sourced statement that says when a matching quote does NOT require approval. Statement_b never says a matching quote can skip approval.

The workflow's hard cap of 10 approvers and its All-or-at-least-one requirement both presuppose that the approver list can be shorter than it was configured. A removal rule is the only mechanism the research describes for it becoming empty.

This product is not HubSpot. It ships an API, records are arbitrary JSON, and no field is required. So neither statement can be enforced by a missing configuration: a room with one approver is a legitimate configuration this product must let work.

candidate_1.rule: At enrolment, drop every approver who created the quote. If approvers remain, they must approve and the creator may not vote. If none remain, the quote needs no approval and is publishable immediately. The enrolment record names the removal and the reason.
candidate_1.risk: A one-approver discount policy self-approves. That is the policy that configuration chose.

candidate_2.rule: Every matching quote requires approval. The creator is dropped from the approver list. If that empties the list, the enrolment is refused with a named reason and the quote stays DRAFT and unshareable until a second approver is configured.
candidate_2.satisfies: Statement_b, and contradicts the only sourced sentence that describes skipping approval.
candidate_2.risk: A room with one approver can never publish a discounted quote. The workflow deadlocks its own stated use case.

constraints: The chosen reading must be served on the page so a reviewer sees it rather than trusting a docstring.
Records are arbitrary JSON. No migration and no typed column.
The domain module imports nothing but the store.

best_rule.instructions: Considering the two conflicting sourced sentences and the measured context, which candidate should this workflow implement? Judge on fidelity to the evidence, on whether the workflow can operate at all in a one-approver room, and on whether one rule can satisfy both sentences.

criteria.enrolment_removal: At enrolment drop the creator from the approver list. Remaining approvers vote. An emptied list means no approval is required and the quote publishes.
criteria.strict_no_own_vote: Every match requires approval. Drop the creator from the list. An emptied list is refused and the quote stays DRAFT and unshareable.

state.change_summary: Route a discounted quote for standard approval. A configured rule of property filters and up to ten approvers is evaluated at submit, publish and share. The quote is enrolled, each approver approves or requests changes, and only an approved quote can be shared. The creator is removed from the approver list at enrolment, so a sole-approver author needs no approval and nobody can approve their own quote. Six new files in a new domain package, a new feature module, two test files and a new frontend folder. No shared file edited.

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main?
